title: Proactive throttle policy for multi-tier regional routing
creator: Alina Romero
description: Goal: Build a proactive throttling and admission policy that prioritizes requests across free/paid/enterprise tiers while making region-aware decisions and seamlessly falling back to lower-cost model variants when quota pressure or regional congestion occurs. This ticket defines the algorithm, data signals, and rollout/observability plan.
background: Current tier routing is reactive: quotas are enforced at admission time and fallbacks are applied per-request with limited coordination across regions. This leads to poor tail latency under contention (head-of-line issues), uneven regional degradation, and expensive last-minute cross-region failovers. The objective is to make admission decisions earlier and probabilistically smooth demand so higher-tier SLAs remain stable while free-tier requests are deferred or probabilistically downgraded under load.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement a per-tenant/per-organization budget window that decays over a configurable window (default 60s) and contributes to an admission score
2) Admission score combines tier_weight, remaining_budget_ratio, region_health_score, and model_variant_cost_factor into a single scalar used for probabilistic admission

3) When regional capacity < threshold, requests should be steered to compatible fallback regions or downgraded to cheaper quantized/shorter-context variants without increasing client error rate > 1% above baseline
4) Expose metrics: admitted_rate_by_tier, rejected_rate_by_tier, average_lat_p90_by_tier, fallback_rate_by_variant, cross_region_failover_count
5) Feature gated and rolloutable per-account via Console (canary, percentage rollout, and emergency disable)
6) Automated integration tests that simulate multi-region overload and assert graceful degradation behavior
technical_approach: 1) Signals: per-tenant quota windows, regional node utilization, per-model variant cost estimate, observed tail latency. 2) Admission algorithm: compute admission_score = w_tier*tier_score + w_budget*budget_score + w_region*region_score - w_cost*cost_penalty. Translate score to probability p = sigmoid(scale*(score - threshold)). 3) Soft-throttling: sample admission using p; if denied, attempt immediate low-latency fallback path (e.g., quantized model or cached prefix) or enqueue with bounded short backoff for free-tier. 4) Circuit heuristics: open circuit for region if error_rate > X% or p90 latency > SLO for T seconds. 5) Coordination: lightweight gossip of region health and quota-burn signals across frontends to avoid simultaneous mass failovers. 6) Observability: add traces for routing decisions, tag requests with admission_score and chosen_variant
implementation_notes:
- We'll add a new RouterV2 hook in the serving runtime that returns (admit|fallback|redirect) decisions. RouterV2 will be config-driven (weights, thresholds, decay windows).
- Budget windows stored in Redis with sliding-token semantics and TTL; consider migrating to local approximate counters for extreme scale.
- Fallback variants must carry fidelity tags so Console and Optimize can measure quality regressions.
- Add safety net: enterprise tier with emergency reserve pool that can preempt queued lower-tier requests when reserve_policy enabled.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off by default. 2) Internal canary with test tenants for two weeks. 3) Gradual 10/30/60 rollout to free-tier-heavy regions while monitoring admittance and latency metrics. 4) Enable emergency kill-switch in Console and SD oncall runbook. 5) Post-rollout 2-week observation window and automated rollback criteria defined (latency delta, error delta, fallback regression)
privacy_and_security_considerations: Quota and routing metadata are PII-free but must comply with tenant isolation. Router decisions include tenant IDs only in internal traces; traces sampled 1% for long-term storage. Security review required because we add config controls that can route across regions and may surface policy decisions in logs.
open_questions: Should budget windows be per-project or per-org? Recommendation: start per-project and add per-org aggregation later.
What default weights should we pick for tier vs budget vs region? Proposed starting point: tier=0.6, budget=0.25, region=0.15.
Do we allow free-tier queuing or always return a fast denial+fallback? Proposal: hybrid — short bounded queue (200ms) then fallback/deny.
Operational cost: do we allow cross-region failovers for paid tier before exhausting local reserved capacity?
updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed — prototype admission_score computed and locally validated against traffic replay. Observed 18% reduction in tail latency for paid-tier requests during simulated overload.

2025-02-15: Design review with PM and SRE. Decided to implement budget windows using Redis tokens with fallback to local approximate counters if Redis latency spikes. PM requested additional dashboard tiles for fallback quality impact.
2025-02-18: Security requested explicit consent for cross-region routing in enterprise contracts. Added security_review_required flag and added contract check to rollout gating.

2025-02-21: Began integrating RouterV2 hook into serving runtime; initial unit tests for probabilistic admission added. Feature flag scaffolding merged into trunk (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1492).
review_feedback: SRE: ensure that gossip adds minimal bandwidth — use heartbeat summaries not full state.
PM: require per-tenant visibility in Console with sample requests showing why a request was downgraded.
Design: include user-facing messaging for API clients when fallbacks occur (structured reason codes).
Engineering: add deterministic seeds for probabilistic admission in tests to avoid flakiness.
